# Test PGO optimizations/bug-fixes in Tango

# this test rebuild runtime with different flags, skip in short mode
[short] skip

# generate cpu.prof
go run test_recursive.go

# build with PGO's default flow, checking diagnostics of the current package is sufficient
go build -pgo ./cpu.prof -gcflags='-d=pgodebug=1' test_recursive.go
stderr 'check allows inlining for call reflect.Value.Len'
# to warn if upstream branch supports recursive inlining, someday
! stderr 'check allows inlining for call reflect.Value.lenNonSlice'

# build with the resursive enhancement flow
go build -pgo ./cpu.prof -gcflags='-d=pgodebug=1,pgorecursive=1' test_recursive.go
stderr 'check allows inlining for call reflect.Value.Len'
stderr 'check allows inlining for call reflect.Value.lenNonSlice'

-- prof --
-- test_recursive.go --
package main

import (
  "log"
  "os"
  "runtime/pprof"
  "reflect"
  "time"
)

func main() {
  f, err := os.Create("cpu.prof")
  if err != nil {
    log.Fatal("fail to create CPU profile: ", err)
  }
  defer f.Close()

  if err := pprof.StartCPUProfile(f); err != nil {
    log.Fatal("fail to start CPU profile: ", err)
  }
  defer pprof.StopCPUProfile()

  t := time.Now()
  // approximately 1 second
  benchStringLen(1000000*300)
  d := time.Now().Sub(t)
  log.Printf("total length: %d, cost: %v\n", total, d)
}

var v reflect.Value
var s string
var total int

//go:noinline
func benchStringLen(n int) {
  s = "hello pgo"
  v = reflect.ValueOf(s)

  for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
    total += v.Len()
  }
}
